text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-p99-latency spike detected for prod-route /v1/generate at 18:24 UTC — p99 jumped to ~1.8s, p95 ~420ms. Auto-page to oncall (ryan) triggered.
ryan: seeing it, joining. can someone grab dashboards?
maya: looking at trace and kvcache metrics now. initial thought: sudden increase in tail latencies for streaming responses.
ashley: tagging ops — I can check infra autoscaling and recent deploys. @sandeep FYI re: any model changes?
sandeep: no model rollout in last 24h. we had a background quantization job yesterday but it finished earlier. not aware of config flips.
jordan: metrics snapshot:
```
# quick numbers from live-dash
p50 85ms
p95 420ms
p99 1.8s -> baseline ~650ms
streaming stalls count +62% in last 3m
kvcache hit-rate dropped from 93% -> 72%
```
maya: kv cache drop correlates with increased miss latency. investigating whether cache eviction kicked in.
ryan: quick checks: any region-specific flare? looks global but slightly heavier in us-west-2.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-87321 assigned to ryan.
ryan: initiating quick mitigation: enabling degraded-routing to fallback-model small-ish variant and increasing worker concurrency on dedicated pools for route /v1/generate. Will post commands.
ryan: commands run: `redwood route set-fallback --route /v1/generate --model rwd-small-qa-v2` and `infra scale-pool gen-prod-west2 --delta +20%`
maya: running a KV cache restore scan for hot prefixes. found a hot prefix churn pattern — some clients sending long prefix prompts causing cache key fragmentation. proposing to enable prefix-coalescing for 10m.
sandeep: prefix-coalescing toggle: `runtime-config set routing.prefix_coalesce=true --route /v1/generate --ttl 600s` — gonna enable after approvals.
ashley: infra note: a noisy tenant in west2 caused small OOM hits on some instances which caused cache evictions. Isolating that tenant to burst pool.
jordan: user-facing impact: brief increase in latency for streaming sessions, small fraction of requests hit p99; overall success rate unchanged. No reported errors from top customers yet.
ryan: temporary mitigations in place. monitoring a/b: fallback model reducing p99 to ~820ms after 30s. p95 down to 360ms.
incident-bot: Status update: mitigated->partial, paging remains open.
maya: after coalescing and isolating noisy tenant, KV hit-rate back to 90% in west2, global p99 now ~700ms.
sandeep: rolling a small runtime flag to reduce continuous-batch size for streaming to avoid head-of-line stalls: `runtime-config set batching.max_inflight_tokens=1024`
ryan: good work team. plan: keep mitigations for 15m, validate with canary traffic, then roll back fallback once stable.
ashley: opening a post-incident ticket with steps: root-cause hypothesis = cache eviction cascading from tenant-driven memory pressure -> kvcache miss spike -> increased decoding latency and streaming stalls.
jordan: customer impact note for CS: elevated latency for a small % of streaming sessions between 18:24-18:38 UTC, recommend pro-active note if customers ask.
incident-bot: Closing note: will update on internal incident board and assign follow-up to eng-runtime (ticket RT-1129).
ryan: thumbs up, leaving oncall to maya in 20m for follow-through. @maya please own the postmortem runbook and assign owners for cache tuning and tenant isolation.
maya: copying runbook checklist now. I will kick off the postmortem and add logs/traces: `pm run start --id RT-1129`.
ryan: thanks — marking as handoff complete, I'm unassigning PD.
pagerduty-bot: PD-87321 resolved by ryan at 18:36 UTC.
incident-bot: last update at 18:36 UTC — monitoring continues.
